NASB.1: Now it came about, when men began to multiply on the face of the land, and daughters were born to them,
NASB.2: that the sons of God saw that the daughters of men were beautiful; and they took wives for themselves, whomever they chose.
NASB.3: Then the LORD said, 'My Spirit shall not strive with man forever, because he also is flesh; nevertheless his days shall be one hundred and twenty years.'
NASB.4: The Nephilim were on the earth in those days, and also afterward, when the sons of God came in to the daughters of men, and they bore [children] to them. Those were the mighty men who [were] of old, men of renown.
NASB.5: Then the LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great on the earth, and that every intent of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.
NASB.6: The LORD was sorry that He had made man on the earth, and He was grieved in His heart.
NASB.7: The LORD said, 'I will blot out man whom I have created from the face of the land, from man to animals to creeping things and to birds of the sky; for I am sorry that I have made them.'
NASB.8: But Noah found favor in the eyes of the LORD.
NASB.9: These are [the records of] the generations of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his time; Noah walked with God.
NASB.10: Noah became the father of three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
NASB.11: Now the earth was corrupt in the sight of God, and the earth was filled with violence.
NASB.12: God looked on the earth, and behold, it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted their way upon the earth.
NASB.13: Then God said to Noah, 'The end of all flesh has come before Me; for the earth is filled with violence because of them; and behold, I am about to destroy them with the earth.
NASB.14: 'Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood; you shall make the ark with rooms, and shall cover it inside and out with pitch.
NASB.15: 'This is how you shall make it: the length of the ark three hundred cubits, its breadth fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.
NASB.16: 'You shall make a window for the ark, and finish it to a cubit from the top; and set the door of the ark in the side of it; you shall make it with lower, second, and third decks.
NASB.17: 'Behold, I, even I am bringing the flood of water upon the earth, to destroy all flesh in which is the breath of life, from under heaven; everything that is on the earth shall perish.
NASB.18: 'But I will establish My covenant with you; and you shall enter the ark-- you and your sons and your wife, and your sons' wives with you.
NASB.19: 'And of every living thing of all flesh, you shall bring two of every [kind] into the ark, to keep [them] alive with you; they shall be male and female.
NASB.20: 'Of the birds after their kind, and of the animals after their kind, of every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, two of every [kind] will come to you to keep [them] alive.
NASB.21: 'As for you, take for yourself some of all food which is edible, and gather [it] to yourself; and it shall be for food for you and for them.'
NASB.22: Thus Noah did; according to all that God had commanded him, so he did.

NKJV.1: Now it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born to them,
NKJV.2: that the sons of God saw the daughters of men, that they were beautiful; and they took wives for themselves of all whom they chose.
NKJV.3: And the LORD said, “My Spirit shall not strive with man forever, for he is indeed flesh; yet his days shall be one hundred and twenty years.”
NKJV.4: There were giants on the earth in those days, and also afterward, when the sons of God came in to the daughters of men and they bore children to them. Those were the mighty men who were of old, men of renown.
NKJV.5: Then the LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every intent of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.
NKJV.6: And the LORD was sorry that He had made man on the earth, and He was grieved in His heart.
NKJV.7: So the LORD said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth, both man and beast, creeping thing and birds of the air, for I am sorry that I have made them.”
NKJV.8: But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.
NKJV.9: This is the genealogy of Noah. Noah was a just man, perfect in his generations. Noah walked with God.
NKJV.10: And Noah begot three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
NKJV.11: The earth also was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.
NKJV.12: So God looked upon the earth, and indeed it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted their way on the earth.
NKJV.13: And God said to Noah, “The end of all flesh has come before Me, for the earth is filled with violence through them; and behold, I will destroy them with the earth.
NKJV.14: Make yourself an ark of gopherwood; make rooms in the ark, and cover it inside and outside with pitch.
NKJV.15: And this is how you shall make it: The length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.
NKJV.16: You shall make a window for the ark, and you shall finish it to a cubit from above; and set the door of the ark in its side. You shall make it with lower, second, and third decks.
NKJV.17: And behold, I Myself am bringing floodwaters on the earth, to destroy from under heaven all flesh in which is the breath of life; everything that is on the earth shall die.
NKJV.18: But I will establish My covenant with you; and you shall go into the ark—you, your sons, your wife, and your sons’ wives with you.
NKJV.19: And of every living thing of all flesh you shall bring two of every sort into the ark, to keep them alive with you; they shall be male and female.
NKJV.20: Of the birds after their kind, of animals after their kind, and of every creeping thing of the earth after its kind, two of every kind will come to you to keep them alive.
NKJV.21: And you shall take for yourself of all food that is eaten, and you shall gather it to yourself; and it shall be food for you and for them.”
NKJV.22: Thus Noah did; according to all that God commanded him, so he did.

ESV.1: When man began to multiply on the face of the land and daughters were born to them,
ESV.2: the sons of God saw that the daughters of man were attractive. And they took as their wives any they chose.
ESV.3: Then the LORD said, “My Spirit shall not abide in  man forever, for he is flesh: his days shall be 120 years.”
ESV.4: The Nephilim  were on the earth in those days, and also afterward, when the sons of God came in to the daughters of man and they bore children to them. These were the mighty men who were of old, the men of renown.
ESV.5: The LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every intention of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.
ESV.6: And the LORD regretted that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him to his heart.
ESV.7: So the LORD said, “I will blot out man whom I have created from the face of the land, man and animals and creeping things and birds of the heavens, for I am sorry that I have made them.”
ESV.8: But Noah found favor in the eyes of the LORD.
ESV.9: These are the generations of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation. Noah walked with God.
ESV.10: And Noah had three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
ESV.11: Now the earth was corrupt in God's sight, and the earth was filled with violence.
ESV.12: And God saw the earth, and behold, it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted their way on the earth.
ESV.13: And God said to Noah, “I have determined to make an end of all flesh,  for the earth is filled with violence through them. Behold, I will destroy them with the earth.
ESV.14: Make yourself an ark of gopher wood.  Make rooms in the ark, and cover it inside and out with pitch.
ESV.15: This is how you are to make it: the length of the ark 300 cubits,  its breadth 50 cubits, and its height 30 cubits.
ESV.16: Make a roof  for the ark, and finish it to a cubit above, and set the door of the ark in its side. Make it with lower, second, and third decks.
ESV.17: For behold, I will bring a flood of waters upon the earth to destroy all flesh in which is the breath of life under heaven. Everything that is on the earth shall die.
ESV.18: But I will establish my covenant with you, and you shall come into the ark, you, your sons, your wife, and your sons' wives with you.
ESV.19: And of every living thing of all flesh, you shall bring two of every sort into the ark to keep them alive with you. They shall be male and female.
ESV.20: Of the birds according to their kinds, and of the animals according to their kinds, of every creeping thing of the ground, according to its kind, two of every sort shall come in to you to keep them alive.
ESV.21: Also take with you every sort of food that is eaten, and store it up. It shall serve as food for you and for them.”
ESV.22: Noah did this; he did all that God commanded him.

WEB.1: When men began to multiply on the surface of the ground, and daughters were born to them,
WEB.2: God’s sons saw that men’s daughters were beautiful, and they took any that they wanted for themselves as wives.
WEB.3: Yahweh said, “My Spirit will not strive with man forever, because he also is flesh; so his days will be one hundred twenty years.”
WEB.4: The Nephilim  were in the earth in those days, and also after that, when God’s sons came in to men’s daughters and had children with them. Those were the mighty men who were of old, men of renown.
WEB.5: Yahweh saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of man’s heart was continually only evil.
WEB.6: Yahweh was sorry that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him in his heart.
WEB.7: Yahweh said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the surface of the ground — man, along with animals, creeping things, and birds of the sky — for I am sorry that I have made them.”
WEB.8: But Noah found favor in Yahweh’s eyes.
WEB.9: This is the history of the generations of Noah: Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time. Noah walked with God.
WEB.10: Noah became the father of three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
WEB.11: The earth was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.
WEB.12: God saw the earth, and saw that it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted their way on the earth.
WEB.13: God said to Noah, “I will bring an end to all flesh, for the earth is filled with violence through them. Behold, I will destroy them and the earth.
WEB.14: Make a ship of gopher wood. You shall make rooms in the ship, and shall seal it inside and outside with pitch.
WEB.15: This is how you shall make it. The length of the ship shall be three hundred cubits,  its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.
WEB.16: You shall make a roof in the ship, and you shall finish it to a cubit upward. You shall set the door of the ship in its side. You shall make it with lower, second, and third levels.
WEB.17: I, even I, do bring the flood of waters on this earth, to destroy all flesh having the breath of life from under the sky. Everything that is in the earth will die.
WEB.18: But I will establish my covenant with you. You shall come into the ship, you, your sons, your wife, and your sons’ wives with you.
WEB.19: Of every living thing of all flesh, you shall bring two of every sort into the ship, to keep them alive with you. They shall be male and female.
WEB.20: Of the birds after their kind, of the livestock after their kind, of every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, two of every sort will come to you, to keep them alive.
WEB.21: Take with you some of all food that is eaten, and gather it to yourself; and it will be for food for you, and for them.”
WEB.22: Thus Noah did. He did all that God commanded him.

NLT.1: Then the people began to multiply on the earth, and daughters were born to them.
NLT.2: The sons of God saw the beautiful women and took any they wanted as their wives.
NLT.3: Then the LORD said, “My Spirit will not put up with humans for such a long time, for they are only mortal flesh. In the future, their normal lifespan will be no more than 120 years.”
NLT.4: In those days, and for some time after, giant Nephilites lived on the earth, for whenever the sons of God had intercourse with women, they gave birth to children who became the heroes and famous warriors of ancient times.
NLT.5: The LORD observed the extent of human wickedness on the earth, and he saw that everything they thought or imagined was consistently and totally evil.
NLT.6: So the LORD was sorry he had ever made them and put them on the earth. It broke his heart.
NLT.7: And the LORD said, “I will wipe this human race I have created from the face of the earth. Yes, and I will destroy every living thing — all the people, the large animals, the small animals that scurry along the ground, and even the birds of the sky. I am sorry I ever made them.”
NLT.8: But Noah found favor with the LORD.
NLT.9: This is the account of Noah and his family. Noah was a righteous man, the only blameless person living on earth at the time, and he walked in close fellowship with God.
NLT.10: Noah was the father of three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
NLT.11: Now God saw that the earth had become corrupt and was filled with violence.
NLT.12: God observed all this corruption in the world, for everyone on earth was corrupt.
NLT.13: So God said to Noah, “I have decided to destroy all living creatures, for they have filled the earth with violence. Yes, I will wipe them all out along with the earth!
NLT.14: “Build a large boat from cypress wood and waterproof it with tar, inside and out. Then construct decks and stalls throughout its interior.
NLT.15: Make the boat 450 feet long, 75 feet wide, and 45 feet high.
NLT.16: Leave an 18-inch opening below the roof all the way around the boat. Put the door on the side, and build three decks inside the boat — lower, middle, and upper.
NLT.17: “Look! I am about to cover the earth with a flood that will destroy every living thing that breathes. Everything on earth will die.
NLT.18: But I will confirm my covenant with you. So enter the boat — you and your wife and your sons and their wives.
NLT.19: Bring a pair of every kind of animal — a male and a female — into the boat with you to keep them alive during the flood.
NLT.20: Pairs of every kind of bird, and every kind of animal, and every kind of small animal that scurries along the ground, will come to you to be kept alive.
NLT.21: And be sure to take on board enough food for your family and for all the animals.”
NLT.22: So Noah did everything exactly as God had commanded him.

CSB17.1: When mankind began to multiply on the earth and daughters were born to them,
CSB17.2: the sons of God <sup>ⓘ</sup> saw that the daughters of mankind were beautiful, and they took any they chose as wives <sup>[1]</sup> for themselves. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.3: And the LORD said, “My Spirit will not remain <sup>[2]</sup> with <sup>[3]</sup> mankind forever, <sup>ⓚ</sup> because they are corrupt. <sup>[4]</sup> <sup>ⓛ</sup> Their days will be 120 years.”
CSB17.4: The Nephilim <sup>[5]</sup> were on the earth both in those days and afterward, when the sons of God came to the daughters of mankind, who bore children to them. They were the powerful men of old, the famous men.
CSB17.5: When the LORD saw that human wickedness was widespread on the earth and that every inclination of the human mind was nothing but evil all the time, <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.6: the LORD regretted that he had made man on the earth, <sup>ⓝ</sup> and he was deeply grieved. <sup>[6]</sup>
CSB17.7: Then the LORD said, “I will wipe mankind, whom I created, off the face of the earth, together with the animals, creatures that crawl, and birds of the sky — for I regret that I made them.”
CSB17.8: Noah, however, found favor with the LORD. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.9: These are the family records <sup>ⓑ</sup> of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, <sup>ⓒ</sup> blameless among his contemporaries; <sup>ⓓ</sup> Noah walked with God. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.10: And Noah fathered three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
CSB17.11: Now the earth was corrupt in God’s sight, and the earth was filled with wickedness. <sup>[7]</sup>
CSB17.12: God saw how corrupt the earth was, for every creature had corrupted its way on the earth. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.13: Then God said to Noah, “I have decided to put an end to every creature, for the earth is filled with wickedness because of them; therefore I am going to destroy them along with the earth.
CSB17.14: “Make yourself an ark of gopher <sup>[8]</sup> wood. Make rooms in the ark, and cover it with pitch inside and outside.
CSB17.15: This is how you are to make it: The ark will be 450 feet long, 75 feet wide, and 45 feet high. <sup>[9]</sup>
CSB17.16: You are to make a roof, <sup>[10]</sup> finishing the sides of the ark to within eighteen inches <sup>[11]</sup> of the roof. You are to put a door in the side of the ark. Make it with lower, middle, and upper decks.
CSB17.17: “Understand that I am bringing a flood — floodwaters on the earth <sup>ⓖ</sup> to destroy every creature under heaven with the breath of life in it. Everything on earth will perish.
CSB17.18: But I will establish my covenant with you, <sup>ⓗ</sup> and you will enter the ark with your sons, your wife, and your sons’ wives.
CSB17.19: You are also to bring into the ark two of all the living creatures, male and female, to keep them alive with you.
CSB17.20: Two of everything — from the birds according to their kinds, from the livestock according to their kinds, and from the animals that crawl on the ground according to their kinds — will come to you so that you can keep them alive.
CSB17.21: Take with you every kind of food that is eaten; gather it as food for you and for them.”
CSB17.22: And Noah did this. He did everything that God had commanded him. <sup>ⓘ</sup>

AMP.1: Now it happened, when men began to multiply on the face of the land, and daughters were born to them,
AMP.2: that the sons of God saw that the daughters of men were beautiful and desirable; and they took wives for themselves, whomever they chose and desired.
AMP.3: Then the LORD said, "My Spirit shall not strive and remain with man forever, because he is indeed flesh [sinful, corrupt—given over to sensual appetites]; nevertheless his days shall yet be a hundred and twenty years."
AMP.4: There were Nephilim (men of stature, notorious men) on the earth in those days—and also afterward—when the sons of God lived with the daughters of men, and they gave birth to their children. These were the mighty men who were of old, men of renown (great reputation, fame).
AMP.5: The LORD saw that the wickedness (depravity) of man was great on the earth, and that every imagination or intent of the thoughts of his heart were only evil continually.
AMP.6: The LORD regretted that He had made mankind on the earth, and He was [deeply] grieved in His heart.
AMP.7: So the LORD said, "I will destroy (annihilate) mankind whom I have created from the surface of the earth—not only man, but the animals and the crawling things and the birds of the air—because it [deeply] grieves Me [to see mankind's sin] and I regret that I have made them."
AMP.8: But Noah found favor and grace in the eyes of the LORD.
AMP.9: These are the records of the generations (family history) of Noah. Noah was a righteous man [one who was just and had right standing with God], blameless in his [evil] generation; Noah walked (lived) [in habitual fellowship] with God.

NIV.1:
The Flood
When men began to increase in number on the earth and daughters were born to them,
NIV.2: the sons of God saw that the daughters of men were beautiful, and they married any of them they chose.
NIV.3: Then the Lord said, “My Spirit will not contend with man forever, for he is mortal; his days will be a hundred and twenty years.”
NIV.4: The Nephilim were on the earth in those days—and also afterward—when the sons of God went to the daughters of men and had children by them. They were the heroes of old, men of renown.
NIV.5: The Lord saw how great man’s wickedness on the earth had become, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil all the time.
NIV.6: The Lord was grieved that he had made man on the earth, and his heart was filled with pain.
NIV.7: So the Lord said, “I will wipe mankind, whom I have created, from the face of the earth—men and animals, and creatures that move along the ground, and birds of the air—for I am grieved that I have made them.”
NIV.8: But Noah found favor in the eyes of the Lord.
NIV.9:
This is the account of Noah.
Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time, and he walked with God.
NIV.10: Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth.
NIV.11: Now the earth was corrupt in God’s sight and was full of violence.
NIV.12: God saw how corrupt the earth had become, for all the people on earth had corrupted their ways.
NIV.13: So God said to Noah, “I am going to put an end to all people, for the earth is filled with violence because of them. I am surely going to destroy both them and the earth.
NIV.14: So make yourself an ark of cypress wood; make rooms in it and coat it with pitch inside and out.
NIV.15: This is how you are to build it: The ark is to be 450 feet long, 75 feet wide and 45 feet high.
NIV.16: Make a roof for it and finish the ark to within 18 inches of the top. Put a door in the side of the ark and make lower, middle and upper decks.
NIV.17: I am going to bring floodwaters on the earth to destroy all life under the heavens, every creature that has the breath of life in it. Everything on earth will perish.
NIV.18: But I will establish my covenant with you, and you will enter the ark—you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with you.
NIV.19: You are to bring into the ark two of all living creatures, male and female, to keep them alive with you.
NIV.20: Two of every kind of bird, of every kind of animal and of every kind of creature that moves along the ground will come to you to be kept alive.
NIV.21: You are to take every kind of food that is to be eaten and store it away as food for you and for them.”
NIV.22: Noah did everything just as God commanded him.
